takeaway: Amoebic dysentery: Entamoeba histolytica from contaminated food and water causes fever and bloody diarrhoea with an abnormal colonic mucosa after travel.

question.text: A 70-year-old man recently returned from Bangladesh is admitted with a high temperature and persistent bloody diarrhoea with a grossly abnormal rectal mucosa on sigmoidoscopy. Diagnosis?
question.say: A seventy-year-old man has just returned from Bangladesh. He is admitted with a high temperature and persistent bloody diarrhoea, and sigmoidoscopy shows a grossly abnormal rectal mucosa. What is the likely diagnosis?

lines.say: This seventy-year-old traveller has just come home from Bangladesh.
He looks sweaty and miserable, clutching his tummy.
The thermometer is burning. He has a high fever.

lines.text: Sigmoidoscopy: a grossly abnormal rectal mucosa.
lines.say: The sigmoidoscope shows a raw, grossly abnormal rectal mucosa. The sigmoid colon is a favourite site.
The stowaway on his suitcase is Entamoeba histolytica, caught from contaminated food and water.

lines.text: Remember: fever and bloody diarrhoea after travel is amoebic dysentery.
lines.say: Remember: fever and bloody diarrhoea after travel point to amoebic dysentery.
